brief: A caddy for next to my kitchen sink: a dispenser that pours out bleach for wiping the counters, plus two bins for sponges.

requirements.evidence: 2-cell build (piece:0,0,0;full, piece:0,1,0;full) sized for beside sink; check_build ok, meshClash clear
requirements.requirement: Caddy for next to kitchen sink

requirements.evidence: No dispenser/pour/spout/bottle part in catalog; 3D-printed plastic with fit-only checks cannot be made bleach-safe (chemical resistance, leak-proofing unverifiable). Nothing built for bleach.
requirements.requirement: Dispenser that pours out bleach for wiping counters

requirements.evidence: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-drain and bin:0,1,0~hex-bin-full-drain — two drained full-depth bins

finish.summary: Built a 2-cell caddy with two drained bins for sponges. Did not build the bleach pourer: no such part exists and printed plastic cannot be verified bleach-safe — use a store-bought bleach dispenser instead.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
